t.6.86.1: But when Mahodara had been slain, the mighty Mahāpārśva threw the fearsome army of Aṅgada into turmoil with his arrows.
t.6.86.2: He struck the heads of the foremost monkeys from their bodies on every side, as the wind makes a fruit fall from its stalk.
t.6.86.3: With his arrows the rākṣasa cut off the arms and shoulders of some of the vānaras, and, greatly enraged, he tore open the sides of others.
t.6.86.4: Those monkeys, tormented by the shower of arrows from Mahāpārśva, all became senseless, their faces turned away in despair.
t.6.86.5: Seeing the army agitated and harassed by the rākṣasas, mighty-armed Aṅgada surged forth with great force, like the ocean on the day of the full moon.
t.6.86.6: Seizing an iron club that shone like the rays of the sun, the best of monkeys brought it down upon Mahāpārśva in battle.
t.6.86.7: Stunned by that blow, Mahāpārśva, together with his charioteer, fell senseless from that chariot to the ground.
t.6.86.8: But that king of the bears, splendid and of exceedingly great valour, resembling a heap of dark collyrium, sprang forth from his own troop, which looked like a mass of clouds.
t.6.86.9: Enraged, he seized a huge rock resembling a mountain peak, swiftly struck down the horses with it, and shattered that chariot.
t.6.86.10: After a moment, the mighty Mahāpārśva regained consciousness and in turn pierced Aṅgada again with many arrows.
t.6.86.12: Seeing Gavākṣa and Jāmbavant tormented by arrows, Aṅgada, overwhelmed with rage, seized a terrible iron club.
t.6.86.11: He struck Jāmbavant in the middle of the chest with three arrows, and he struck the king of the bears and Gavākṣa with many shafts.
t.6.86.13: Enraged, Aṅgada turned upon that iron club of the rākṣasa standing at a distance, a club that shone with a radiance like the rays of the sun.
t.6.86.14: Grasping it with both arms and whirling it around, the swift son of Vālin hurled it at Mahāpārśva to kill him.
t.6.86.16: Rushing upon him with great speed, the mighty son of Vālin, enraged, struck him with the flat of his hand at the root of his ear, where the earring hung.
t.6.86.15: That iron bar, hurled by the mighty one, knocked the bow with its arrow from the hand of that rākṣasa, and struck down his helmet as well.
t.6.86.17: But the enraged Mahāpārśva, of great speed and great splendour, seized with one hand an enormous battle-axe.
t.6.86.18: Utterly enraged, the rākṣasa hurled that firm, spotless weapon, made of iron and washed with oil, down upon the son of Vālin.
t.6.86.19: Furious, Aṅgada wrenched free the battle-axe that he had brought down violently upon his left shoulder-blade.
t.6.86.20: That hero Aṅgada, equal in valour to his father, exceedingly enraged, clenched his own fist, which resembled a thunderbolt.
t.6.86.21: Knowing the vital points, he brought down his fist, whose impact was like Indra's thunderbolt, upon the rākṣasa near the breast, aimed at the heart.
t.6.86.22: By that blow falling upon him in the great battle, the heart of the rākṣasa quickly burst, and he fell slain upon the earth.
t.6.86.23: When he had fallen to the ground, that army was thrown into turmoil, and in the battle a great wrath arose in Rāvaṇa.
